artifacts.summary: Confirms the origin fix (test-gate-registry-resolution.sh case13, exact-pid kill -0) and the standard's documented gap; corpus audit of agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/** and scripts/*.sh finds zero live violations of the exact-pid rule (search commands and per-file breakdown included, re-runnable); identifies bounded-build-waiter.md as a sibling-but-distinct agent-layer discipline using the same mechanism; recommends prose-only subsection (declines a mechanical lint on 100%-exemption-rate evidence) inserted into the existing '## Suite runtime: --jobs, --timings, and gate selection' section; flags an index-entries.json keyword/topic gap for the implementation phase.

memory_candidates.content: When auditing a shell-test corpus for a process-check anti-pattern (e.g. pgrep -f/pkill -f/ps|grep name-based matching), expect most textual hits to be non-violating: comments documenting the anti-pattern, fixture command strings fed to a hook-under-test that itself validates the pattern in a different context, or tests of a subject's absence of the pattern. A high exemption-rate (most hits need an allowlist entry) is a strong signal to prefer prose-only guidance over a mechanical lint, mirroring the existing lint-state-writer-boundary.sh template's own documented Layer 1/Layer 2 (structural + file-allowlist) limitation.

This repo already codifies 'never match a process by name under concurrency, always capture the exact pid at spawn and check it with kill -0' at the agent-waiter layer (context/patterns/bounded-build-waiter.md Rule 2, enforced by validate-bounded-waiter.sh). The same mechanism recurs at the test-suite-authoring layer for a different hazard (sibling-suite name collision vs. self-match) -- treat these as sibling disciplines for the same underlying mechanism, cross-link them, but never merge them into one rule or one enforcement point, since the actor and hazard differ.
